propositions: MCP transition_ticket and claim_ticket do not expose force, reason, caused_by, and ref parameters that are already supported by the library and CLI, making those capabilities unreachable via MCP.
FastMCP derives tool input schemas and argument models from the handwritten callable signatures in src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py; undeclared parameters are discarded before the callable runs.

The MCP adapter delegate calls forward only close_class for transition_ticket and assignee for claim_ticket, so even if schema fields were added, the parameters would still be lost at the forwarding boundary.

Runtime probes confirmed the root cause: live schemas omit the fields, real registered-tool capture receives only current kwargs, equivalent FastMCP tools with declared fields receive exact sentinels, and MCP ref selects HEAD instead of requested commits.
The 2026-08-18 operator ruling rescinds the force-only CLI policy and mandates force parity across all surfaces (lib/CLI/MCP) with absent certification as the audit signal.
